subtitle: PCSX2
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own setup guide: "[PCSX2 Emulator]" and "A legally-obtained Armored Core 3 ISO - NTSC-U, SLUS-20435". SLUS-20435 is a PS2 US disc serial.
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: the world's own archipelago.json: {"game": "Armored Core 3"}, read 25 Aug 2026.
description: Armored Core 3 as a multiworld. Mission unlocks are shuffled into the item pool. Requires the player's own NTSC-U disc (SLUS-20435) and PCSX2 with PINE enabled on slot 28011.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: PS2 title. The setup guide lists it among the player's own requirements: "A legally-obtained Armored Core 3 ISO".

rom.description: Your own Armored Core 3 disc image for PlayStation 2 -- the NTSC-U release, disc serial SLUS-20435
rom._description_source: the setup guide, word for word: "NTSC-U, SLUS-20435".
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. The guide states none and the world validates nothing about the player's file.

emulator.name: PCSX2
emulator._source: the setup guide links "[PCSX2 Emulator]" without naming a version. No minimum is recorded, because none is stated -- unlike Ratchet & Clank 2, whose guide does state one.

client.name: Armored Core 3 Client
client._name_source: the world's utils.py: `class Constants:` ... `CLIENT_NAME: str = "Armored Core 3 Client"`, which components.py passes to both launch() and Component(). The setup guide names the same string: "Open the Armored Core 3 Client from the Archipelago launcher."
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: components.py builds `Component(Constants.CLIENT_NAME, ..., component_type=Type.CLIENT)` and launches launch_ac3_client, with the transport in the world itself (pine.py and pcsx2_interface.py). Its setup guide's connect sequence is entirely about that client. London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/pcsx2/extension.json declares {"protocol": "pine"}, Systems ["PS2"]. The world speaks PINE itself (pine.py), and the setup guide has the player enable PINE in PCSX2 on slot 28011.
client._lua_note: No Lua. PINE is spoken to PCSX2 directly.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest release read 25 Aug 2026 is v0.1.1, carrying armoredcore3.apworld and a sample YAML.
apworld._world_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"world_version": "0.1.0"}. ⚠ The newest RELEASE tag is v0.1.1, so the world's own file is one step behind its tag. Recorded as the world states it, with the difference visible.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"minimum_ap_version": "0.6.7"}. Our client is 0.6.7, so this is exactly met.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: all 15 .py files in the repository were searched. There is no APPatchExtension, no APProcedurePatch and no patch_file_ending anywhere -- this world produces no patch container at all.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block: the world generates no patch container. The client restructures the mission menu in memory over PINE, which is a client-side action, not a ROM patch.

world_by.name: Aleksandy
world_by._authors_source: the world names them itself: archipelago.json {"authors": ["Aleksandy"]}.
world_by._source: the repository the world is published from; its own source, archipelago.json and setup guide are what this manifest was written against.
world_by._licence_source: the repository has no LICENSE file -- the GitHub API reports license: null (25 Aug 2026). Nothing has been granted explicitly. We redistribute none of this world's code; the player downloads it from the author's own release. Recorded so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.
